notes:
I found good material for vv. 21–25, 30–32 and 36–38. Coverage is thin for vv. 26–29, 33–35 and 39–41, because my tool limits ran out before I could read those verses on Enduring Word and in Coffman (both pages cut off at v. 24 and v. 26). I found nothing from the Catholic, Orthodox or modern-scholarship sites for this passage, so those views are left out. One real dispute between traditions turned up (the birds in v. 32), and so did one critique of prosperity teaching (v. 24).

---

**v. 21**
- **Guzik:** Light by its nature is meant to be shown. Anyone who has God's truth must spread it, just as someone with a cure for a deadly disease must share it. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/mark-4/
- **Coffman (Restoration Movement):** Vv. 21–25 are separate sayings that Jesus has put in a new setting. Here, after hiding His teaching in parables, the lamp shows that the hiding will end. He also links the "stand" to a congregation (Rev 1:20): the believer's lamp belongs in the church. https://studylight.org/commentaries/eng/bcc/mark-4.html
- **Chuck Smith (Calvary Chapel):** You are the light of the world. The light God gives you is meant to light others, not to be kept for yourself. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/mark/4-32.html

**v. 22**
- **Guzik:** Truth, like light, will be revealed. God promises this. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/mark-4/
- **Coffman, quoting Dummelow:** Jesus is correcting a wrong impression the word "mystery" (v. 11) might give. The gospel was kept secret only for a short time, so it could be preached after the Ascension. More broadly, everyone's secrets will be exposed at the final judgment. https://studylight.org/commentaries/eng/bcc/mark-4.html

**v. 23**
- **Chuck Smith:** We can only truly hear when the Spirit opens our ears. He links this to the repeated "he who has an ear" in Revelation. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/mark/4-32.html
- **Desiring God:** One of Jesus' "most repeated sayings in the Gospels is some version of this: 'If anyone has ears to hear, let him hear'". https://www.desiringgod.org/articles/distraction-can-cost-you-everything

**v. 24**
- **Guzik:** Christians should sit under good teachers who teach the whole of God's Word. That should be a major reason for choosing a church. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/mark-4/
- **Gill:** "Measure" was a common Jewish proverb. Here it means that if the disciples listened carefully, worked to understand and passed the teaching on, they would be given more spiritual knowledge. https://www.studylight.org/bible/eng/nkj/mark/4-24.html
- **Barnes:** You shall be treated according to the use you make of your opportunities of learning. https://www.studylight.org/bible/eng/nkj/mark/4-24.html
- **Coffman:** He quotes Euthymius, an early Greek commentator: the attention you give Christ's teaching sets the measure of understanding you receive. Elsewhere Jesus applies the same saying to judging others (Matt 7:2) and to giving (Luke 6:38). https://studylight.org/commentaries/eng/bcc/mark-4.html
- **BibleHub study notes:** The picture is a marketplace measuring vessel. The measure stands for the seriousness and openness we bring to God's word. A guarded or indifferent heart receives little; a receptive heart seeks more of the truth Christ reveals. https://biblehub.com/mark/4-24.htm
- **Prosperity teaching (critique):** Jared Wilson (TGC) says prosperity preachers twist "more will be added" into a formula, as if God's kingdom were some kind of vending machine you just need the passwords for. In his view the "more" is more of Christ. https://www.thegospelcoalition.org/article/the-gospel-is-no-piddlin-thing/
  - For contrast, a BibleHub Q&A page applies the verse to giving money, time and talent ("divine arithmetic," citing Mal 3:10). https://biblehub.com/q/Meaning_of_measure_used_measured_to_you.htm

**v. 25**
- **Coffman:** This is not unfairness to the poor but a lasting law. The diligent student of God's truth is given more; the lazy one forgets even what he knew. He compares the parable of the talents. https://studylight.org/commentaries/eng/bcc/mark-4.html
- **Grant:** Whoever refuses the word, like the three poor soils, loses even what he seemed to have received. https://studylight.org/commentaries/eng/lmg/mark-4.html
- **Desiring God:** If you do not understand, you will lose whatever capacity to understand you *do* have. https://www.desiringgod.org/articles/distraction-can-cost-you-everything

**vv. 26–29**
- **Grant:** After the seed is sown, we must wait patiently. The results come neither quickly nor suddenly, and the growth is the work of the Creator. https://studylight.org/commentaries/eng/lmg/mark-4.html
- **Lange:** God's word keeps ripening even when no one is aware of it. https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/lcc/mark-4.html

**vv. 30–31**
- **Pulpit Commentary:** The kingdom here is the Church, which grew from a tiny start to fill the world. The mustard seed is not literally the smallest seed, but is fairly called so given how much grows from it. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/mark/4-32.html
- **Coffman:** "Smallest" is ordinary exaggeration to make a point. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/mark/4-32.html
- **Light of Israel commentary (citing Wiersbe):** Jesus is teaching about the kingdom, not botany. To His hearers it was the smallest seed they planted. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/mark/4-30.html
- **Constable (quoting Nineham):** The mustard seed warns us not to judge results by how small they start. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/mark/4-30.html

**v. 32: the main point of disagreement (what the birds mean)**
- **Positive reading:**
  - **Barclay:** The church, small at first, has room for every nation. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/mark/4-32.html
  - **Gill:** The birds are saints who find rest under the gospel. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/mark/4-32.html
  - **Biblical Illustrator:** The tree blesses everyone who shelters under it. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/mark/4-32.html
  - **Matthew Henry:** Applies it to grace growing in the soul. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/mark/4-30.html
- **Negative (dispensational) reading:**
  - **Ironside (Plymouth Brethren):** The tree is the Christendom Jesus foresaw, a huge all-inclusive society where Satan's agents (the birds, as in v. 15) find shelter. He compares the trees of Assyria and Babylon in Ezekiel 31 and Daniel 4. https://studylight.org/commentaries/isn/mark-4.html
  - **Chuck Smith:** Calls it unnatural growth, with enemies working inside the church. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/mark/4-30.html
  - **Guzik:** Mentions the positive view, but says this mustard seed plant has grown into a monstrosity, and it harbors birds. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/mark-4/
- **Middle view:** Coffman says the birds are outside activities attached to the kingdom that cannot corrupt it. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/mark/4-32.html

**vv. 33–34**
- **Chuck Smith:** Parables illustrate truth rather than hide it. When the disciples asked, Jesus explained the parables to them in private. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/mark/4-32.html

**vv. 35–36**
- **Constable:** Details such as "that day," "as He was" and the other boats point to an eyewitness, probably Peter. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/mark/4-38.html
- **Ligonier:** Makes the same eyewitness argument. https://learn.ligonier.org/devotionals/jesus-ceases-storm
- **Maclaren:** Many expositors think "as He was" suggests Jesus was worn out after the day's work. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/mark/4-38.htm
- **Barnes:** The other boats probably belonged to people who decided to follow Him. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/mark/4-38.htm

**v. 37**
- **Barnes:** Describes a sudden wind sweeping down over the cliffs, the kind of storm that filled the boat. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/mark/4-38.html

**v. 38**
- **Jesus' sleep shows His real humanity and tiredness:**
  - Guzik: https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/mark-4/
  - Constable: https://www.studylight.org/commentary/mark/4-38.html
  - MacArthur: https://www.gty.org/sermons/41-21/calming-the-storm
  - **Pulpit Commentary:** Jesus slept as man but watched as God. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/mark/4-38.html
- **The cushion:**
  - Vincent: the steersman's leather cushion. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/mark/4-38.htm
  - MacArthur: the Greek word contains the word for "head." https://www.gty.org/sermons/41-21/calming-the-storm
- **The disciples' question:**
  - **Pulpit:** The question sounds impatient, maybe Peter's. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/mark/4-38.html
  - **Ellicott (Anglican):** Only Mark records this despairing complaint, which shows the lack of faith later rebuked. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/mark/4-38.html
  - **JFB:** Unbelief and fear made them forget their place. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/mark/4-38.htm
  - **Matthew Henry:** Christ slept to test their faith and stir up prayer; their faith appeared *weak,* and their prayers *strong.* https://www.studylight.org/commentary/mark/4-38.html
  - **Spurgeon (quoted by Guzik):** "There may be both a sleeping Christ and a sleeping church, but neither Christ nor his church can perish." https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/mark-4/

**v. 40**
- **Guzik:** Jesus could say they had no faith because they accused Him of not caring. Thinking Jesus doesn't care shows unbelief about who He is. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/mark-4/

I found nothing specific on vv. 39 and 41.
